items.title: The Complete Peru: coast, Andes and Amazon

ficha.sub: From the coast to the jungle
ficha.what: A 14-day journey across the coast, the Andes and the Amazon: Lima, Ica, Arequipa, the Colca, Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Tambopata.
ficha.whatLong: Fourteen days to cross Peru's three regions: the Ica desert, the southern Andes with the Colca, Titicaca and Cusco, and the Tambopata jungle.
story: You go up little by little, the way it should be: you start at sea level, pass through Arequipa (2,335 m) and the Colca, and by the time you reach Cusco your body already knows the altitude. At the end, you go down to the jungle.
Along the way you spend a night in a family's home on Amantaní Island, on Lake Titicaca, and two nights in a lodge by the Tambopata River.
ficha.howText: We're with you before, during and after: transfers, trains, overnight buses and someone from our team available 24 hours a day, every day of the trip.
ficha.vivTitle: Fourteen days, from the desert to the jungle.
ficha.vivText: Tap each day to see what you experience and where you sleep.
ficha.chartTitle: From sea level to 5,036 m, and back down to the jungle.
ficha.chartText: The altitude rises in stages: Arequipa, the Colca and Titicaca, before Cusco and Vinicunca. Tap a point on the curve to see each day.

itin.body: We pick you up at the airport. In the afternoon you explore Lima's historic center, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and its markets, tasting 12 Peruvian bites. To finish, a pisco sour if you feel like it.

itin.t: From the sea to the desert
itin.body: Boat to the Ballestas Islands, home to sea lions and Humboldt penguins, passing the Candelabra, a giant drawing in the sand whose origin nobody knows for sure. Lunch at a pisco vineyard and dune buggies with sandboarding in Huacachina until sunset.
Flight to Arequipa and a private tour of its colonial center, built with sillar, a white volcanic stone: that's why it's called the White City. In the background, the Misti volcano.
You cross the Andes to the Colca Canyon, almost twice as deep as the Grand Canyon, and end the day in hot springs. Night in Chivay.
From the Colca viewpoint you watch the Andean condor glide, with a wingspan of up to three meters. Then, the road to Puno, gateway to Titicaca.

You sail Lake Titicaca, the highest navigable lake in the world: first the floating islands of the Uros, handmade from totora reeds, then Amantaní, where you have dinner and sleep in the home of a local family.

itin.t: Taquile and the road to Cusco
itin.body: Taquile Island, where the men knit and the textiles are recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage. At night, bus to Cusco.
Private tour of Cusco, capital of the Inca Empire, where you'll see Inca walls beneath colonial churches. To finish, its viewpoints.

The Maras salt pans, worked since before the Incas; the circular terraces of Moray; the textiles of Chinchero; and Ollantaytambo, an Inca town that is still inhabited. In the afternoon, panoramic train to Aguas Calientes.
Machu Picchu with a private guide: the 15th-century Inca citadel, one of the New Seven Wonders of the World. Return by train and private transfer to Cusco.
Hike to Vinicunca, Rainbow Mountain, above 5,000 m: its stripes come from the minerals in the earth. At night, bus to Puerto Maldonado.
You sail the Tambopata River to the lodge, in one of the most biodiverse places on the planet. Guided jungle walk and a night outing to see monkeys, caimans and birds.
At dawn, hundreds of parrots and macaws arrive at the Chuncho clay lick to eat clay. Then, lakes and jungle trails.
Last morning in the jungle, boat back to Puerto Maldonado and assistance for your departure.

tips: Domestic flights and hotels in Lima, Arequipa, Puno and Cusco are not included: your Travel Advisor quotes them separately.
Take only what you need to the jungle: the rest of your luggage is stored free of charge until you return.
You can board the train to Machu Picchu with hand luggage of up to 5 kg.
plan.access: There are early mornings, two overnight buses and high-altitude hikes (Vinicunca is above 5,000 m). Let us know in advance if you have any medical condition or dietary restriction.

season.text: The coast, the Andes and the jungle have different climates on the same day. From May to September the Andes and the Amazon are in the dry season: clear skies in the highlands and less rain in the jungle; Lima, on the other hand, wakes up gray and cool.

items.title: The Essential Peru, with the Amazon

ficha.what: A 10-day journey through Lima, Ica, Cusco, Machu Picchu and the Tambopata jungle.
ficha.whatLong: A 10-day journey with the essentials of Peru: the flavors of Lima, the Ica desert, Cusco and Machu Picchu, Rainbow Mountain and two nights in the Amazon.
story: Ten days are enough for the desert, the Andes and the jungle if the order is right: first the coast, then Cusco with a free day to acclimatize, and finally the Amazon.
In Cusco and Machu Picchu you have a guide just for you; in the jungle, two nights in a lodge on the Tambopata River.

items.title: The Best of Peru in 9 days

ficha.what: A 9-day journey through Lima, Ica, Cusco and Machu Picchu, with the hikes to Humantay and Vinicunca.
ficha.whatLong: A 9-day journey with the best of the coast and the Andes: Lima, Paracas and Huacachina, Cusco, the Sacred Valley, Machu Picchu, Humantay Lake, a cooking class and Rainbow Mountain.
story: After Machu Picchu comes a free day in Cusco: your body gets used to the altitude before the two big hikes of the trip, Humantay and Vinicunca.
In between, a morning at the market with a chef and a class to cook a Peruvian dish with him.
ficha.howText: From the market to the kitchen: on day 8 you walk through a Cusco market with a chef and cook with him what you bought together.
